description: A dependency-free offline inventory app with validated quantities; this bounded profile does not certify databases, purchasing, accounting, or arbitrary business applications.

task_template.objective: Build a polished offline inventory app satisfying every fixed local-inventory profile requirement.

acceptance_criteria: The page has a main landmark, a visible heading, labeled controls, and a visible status message for invalid input.

A textbox labeled Item name, a spinbutton labeled Quantity, and a button named Add item create an item with a trimmed nonempty name and a safe integer quantity from 0 through 9007199254740991 inclusive.

Every inventory item is an element with data-testid=inventory-item, its literal name, a spinbutton named Quantity followed by the item name, and buttons named Save followed by the item name and Delete followed by the item name.
Editing an item's quantity and pressing its Save button updates only that item; valid zero quantities are accepted.
A searchbox labeled Search items filters visible items by case-insensitive substring of the item name; clearing the query restores all items.
Deleting an item removes only that item. Items and saved quantity changes persist in localStorage and survive a page reload; deletion also persists.

Empty or whitespace-only names, empty quantities, negative quantities, fractional quantities, and quantities outside the safe integer range are rejected without adding or changing an item. Rejected input produces a visible message in a status region.
Names are unique after trimming and case folding; adding a duplicate name must neither create another item nor overwrite the existing quantity.
HTML-looking item names are displayed as literal text and cannot create DOM elements or execute script, including after reload.
The app works offline with only index.html, app.js, and styles.css, without remote assets, package installation, server-side code, or external network access.
The add, edit quantity, search, and delete flow works with Tab, Enter, and Space, and every visible control is reachable by keyboard.

Empty and populated states have no axe-core 4.14.0 WCAG 2 A/AA, WCAG 2.1 A/AA, or WCAG 2.2 AA automated violations or incomplete findings, including color contrast. Normal text needs at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text needs at least 3:1.

Every visible control has a keyboard focus outline at least 2 CSS pixels wide, at least 3:1 contrast against a solid adjacent background, and no clipping or obstruction. Use an opaque solid outline and a nonnegative outline offset.
At viewport widths of 320 and 390 CSS pixels, populated states including a long unbroken item name have no horizontal page overflow or offscreen text or controls.
limitations: The disclosed finite acceptance suite is a regression gate, not proof of arbitrary correctness or resistance to deliberate test gaming.
Browser localStorage is single-browser storage, not a durable database or backup. No identity, cross-device synchronization, transaction accounting, or multi-user inventory is supported.

Automated accessibility checks cover only the declared states and rules. Passing does not certify WCAG conformance, assistive-technology usability, all zoom settings, all browsers, or arbitrary interaction states. Incomplete axe findings fail closed and require repair or a separately designed trusted review process.
The focus check deliberately requires an opaque 2px-or-larger outline over a solid background. Equivalent custom focus designs need a separately verified profile before acceptance.
